subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable auto-cleanup and archival policy for webhook/hook sessions

question: What hook-session lifecycle policy should OpenClaw support for completed webhook agent runs, and how should it interact with generic session maintenance, cron retention, and persistent hook sessions?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent config API, default behavior, transcript deletion or archival semantics, and upgrade safety are product/data-retention decisions.

options.title: Add Explicit Hook Cleanup Policy
options.body: Introduce a default-safe hooks.sessionCleanup-style policy with on-complete, delayed, and never modes plus transcript-retention behavior and focused hook/session tests.

options.title: Rely On Generic Maintenance
options.body: Document that hook sessions are governed only by session.maintenance age/count/disk controls and close the request for hook-specific cleanup.

options.title: Defer Until Persistent Hooks Settle
options.body: Pause cleanup policy until the persistent hook-session direction is settled so cleanup and reuse semantics are designed together.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Hook Cleanup Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce a default-safe hooks.sessionCleanup-style policy with on-complete, delayed, and never modes plus transcript-retention behavior and focused hook/session tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the hook mapping surface and already framed this issue as a maintainer product/API decision.
